_about: One record per customer journey migrated in Gate 4: who read it, what the draft got wrong, what was changed. Generated by scripts/vnext-review.mjs from the reviewer's decision files; the draft generator never writes here.

reviews.note: Human-only route assignment. Draft keyed the instance on subscription+account from the entity prose; the thing entered is the onboarding instance. Cooldown is per instance (none). Pure router: both outcomes are handoffs by design.

Keyed on the requirement, not only the account. The two touches are the exclusive arms of c.self-resolvable (self-resolvable vs someone else's). The specific action carries a destination. One touch per requirement, so no cooldown. Business outcome compared pre/post.

Touch order fixed (final option follows the offer). Offer and confirmation carry destinations. Exit classes corrected: not-eligible and declined are no-action states, no-outcome is a timeout. Waits run from the previous touch. Outcome measured on activation, not on the booking.
Silent close-out. A proxy that is not activation is an invalid-state exit, not a success.
One question per onboarding instance: no cooldown. Not asking is a no-action state. The question carries its form as destination; the wait runs from the ask.

A never-paid relationship is promotional pressure, not lifecycle. Keyed on the lead and its context. Out-of-scope and no-reason are not successes. Success is a meaningful return by the corpus's own rule - the wait advances on it deliberately.
Keyed on the anonymous profile, not on ids it does not yet have. Stale intent is a timeout, not an invalid state.
Pure router by design: every capture ends in a handoff. Keyed on the lead.
Keyed on the person and the entity the intent is about. Noise is a no-action state.
Human routing, not customer communication: both channels are human, pressure class none. One decision per lead action, no cooldown. Pure router. Keyed on the lead.

Keyed on the lead. Recycle and requirement waits are bound to the horizon recorded with the reason, not to the trigger. Exit classes corrected: qualifying and unqualified are no-action states, a terminal mismatch is an invalid state, a lapsed requirement is a timeout.
Named the proxies the trigger must not start on. Keyed on the entity the rule is about and the rule. Both outcomes are correct decisions.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the person and the intent context. The wait is a cooldown by nature; maintained intent is a no-action state.
Keyed on the person and the destination entity. A proxy that is not a conversion is an invalid state, not a suppression.

The graph models the education as one action standing for a bounded sequence, so the local cap is the sequence length the company fixes at entry - a required config, not the plan's action count. The window runs from entry, not from the first touch. No-basis is a no-action state; permission and route loss are suppressions. Progression compared pre/post.
Keyed on the lead and the decline. The re-entry wait is bound to the recorded date. A terminal mismatch is an invalid state.

Keyed on the individual capture. The first touch and the delivery are the exclusive arms of what the person declared. The sequence opener carries the declared subject as destination. Per capture, so no cooldown. Exit classes corrected. Outcome: a destination declared, compared pre/post.
Accepted as drafted; aliases named.
Keyed on the account and the use-case the expectation belongs to. Both exits are no-action states: a miss with nothing behind it is not risk.
Keyed on the relationship the health state is held against. An unexplained deterioration at the end of the diagnostic window is a timeout.
A task to the account owner is not customer pressure: retention priority, pressure class none. Per risk episode, so no cooldown. Keyed on the account and the episode. Monitoring is a no-action state.
Pure router by design: sustained recovery goes to the lifecycle owner, a relapse back to diagnosis. Accepted otherwise.
Keyed on the relationship that ended. Wind-down until the end date is a correct outcome of this journey, not an invalid state.
Keyed on the account and the retention episode. Outcome measured on the relationship recovering, compared pre/post.
Keyed on the person and the purpose-channel-scope the permission is about. Something that is not a permission is an invalid state, not a success.
Accepted as drafted.
Named the proxies the trigger must not start on.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the person and the suppression scope. A released suppression is the journey's success; the persistent one is the suppression state itself.

A contactability repair is service communication, exempt from caps but not security-class. The two prompts are the exclusive arms of c.route and each goes only on a route that still works. Every touch is mandatory, so the discretionary cap is zero. The confirmation carries no call to action by design.
Service class, not security. The confirmation carries the preference centre as its destination. A full opt-out is a no-action outcome for this journey.
The light and heavy asks are the exclusive arms of c.type. The heavy ask carries its contribution route. Not-yet-eligible is a no-action state. One ask, no follow-up.

Keyed on the appeal. An appeal is service communication. Each touch carries the thing it points at; the information request and the outcome are the exclusive arms of c.outcome. Both waits are bound to the appeal deadline. An ineligible appeal is an invalid state. One appeal, no cooldown. Outcome: the review concluding.
Accepted as drafted.

Keyed on the blocked entity and the requirement. Service class. The customer request and the internal request are the exclusive arms of c.provider; the customer request carries where to provide the item. Exit classes corrected: a satisfied requirement is the success, an alternate route is an invalid state for this requirement. Per requirement, no cooldown. The wait is a response window.
Accepted as drafted.

Keyed on the obligation. The reminder carries the discharge route; the number of reminders is the number of thresholds policy defines, a required config. A deadline that passes with the obligation unchanged is a no-action outcome. Outcome compared pre/post.
Accepted as drafted.

The reminder is gated by the pre-deadline wait; the confirmation and the overdue notice follow it as the two arms of the deadline wait. The reminder carries the discharge route; the confirmation carries none by design. The deadline wait is bound to the due date. A moot obligation is a no-action outcome. Outcome compared pre/post.

Keyed on the entity and its grace period. The restricted and quiet notices are the exclusive arms of c.restricted. The final wait routes through c.outcome so the confirmation is a decision, not a send on the success event. The loss notice carries the route back on new terms; the confirmation carries none. Both waits are bound to the grace end. Early termination is an invalid state. The longest path sends three touches.

Keyed on the expired entity and the holder's attempt. The four route statements are the exclusive arms of c.route and each carries its route; the dead end and the confirmation carry none by design. The wait after naming the route is a response window from the touch, not the expiry. At most two touches reach one person. No route back is an invalid state.
Keyed on the account and the entitlement. A pending requirement is a no-action state; a reconciled existing right is a correct outcome.
Keyed on the account and the capability scope. The wait is bound to the suspension's review point.
Keyed on the account and the restoration case. Nothing qualifying for restoration is a no-action state.

Keyed on the account and the restriction. The inform-only and actionable notices are the exclusive arms of c.actionable; the actionable notice carries the resolving condition, the confirmation carries none by design. The wait is bound to the restriction's own deadline. Exit classes corrected. At most two touches. Outcome: the restriction lifted, compared pre/post. Draft purpose text repaired.

Keyed on the entitlement and its holder. The first-time and familiar notices are the exclusive arms of c.first-time; the brief confirmation carries no route by design, the first-time notice and the reminder carry the first action. Both waits are bound to the activation window. At most two touches. Outcome: first use, compared pre/post.

Keyed on the claim. Both requests carry the evidence route and are mandatory; the follow-up request follows the first through the evidence wait. Every touch is mandatory, so the discretionary cap is zero.
Keyed on the verification instance. Each explanation carries the route it names. A terminal basis is a failure outcome.
Keyed on the authentication session. The challenge is mandatory, so the discretionary cap is zero.
An ordinary failure pattern is a no-action outcome.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the recovery case. The proof wait is bound to the recovery window. Further evidence allowed is a no-action state of this instance.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the account and the attribute. A change not verified or invalid leaves the attribute as it was: invalid-state outcomes.
Keyed on the incident. An SLA passing without a conclusion is a timeout outcome.

Keyed on the recovery case. The final wait routes through c.proof so the restoration confirmation is a decision, not a send on the success event. The route issue carries the recovery route; the confirmation carries none by design; the reminder is discretionary. Both waits are bound to the recovery window.
Pending evidence is a no-action state; a rejected link is an invalid state, not a failure of this journey.
Accepted as drafted.
Accepted as drafted.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the account, the member and the role.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the entity and the relationship type it is missing. A policy end state after the SLA is a timeout outcome.

Keyed on the invitation. The known-holder and new-counterparty invitations are the exclusive arms of c.known and both carry the acceptance route; the confirmation carries none by design. Both waits are bound to the invitation's expiry. The longest path sends three touches. A declined invitation is a failure of the ask, not a no-action. Outcome: acceptance, compared pre/post.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the role and the handover. The wait runs to the handover's effective time.

Keyed on the account and the closure request. Every touch is mandatory (transactional), so the discretionary cap is zero. The recoverable and non-recoverable blocker notices are the exclusive arms of c.blockers; the blocker notice carries the blocker, the closure confirmation carries no route by design. Exit classes corrected: an unauthorised request is an invalid state, a blocked closure is a failure of the request.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the account and the closure.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the account.

Keyed on the deletion request. Every touch is mandatory (transactional), so the discretionary cap is zero. The verification request carries the proof route; the two closure records are the exclusive arms of c.outcome and carry no route by design. The decision wait is bound to the obligation's response deadline. An unverified close is an invalid state. Outcome: the deletion resolved.

Keyed on the connection and the failure. The partial and total notices are the exclusive arms of c.scope and both carry the re-authorisation step; the restoration confirmation carries none by design. The revalidation wait is a response window from the notice. Informed-only is a correct outcome; a removed connection is an invalid state. At most two touches. Outcome: revalidation, compared pre/post.

Keyed on the connection attempt. The active confirmation and the generic failure are the exclusive arms of c.outcome; the three stage fixes are the exclusive arms of c.stage and each carries its fix; the confirmation carries none by design. Stage messages repeat through retries, so the local cap is the retry budget the company fixes - a required config. Still-not-connected is a failure; abandonment is a timeout.
An obligation outstanding past its horizon is a timeout outcome.
Named the proxies. A partial satisfaction is a correct reconciliation with the remainder explicit.

Keyed on the refund request. Every touch is mandatory (transactional), so the discretionary cap is zero. Rejection, review and approval are the exclusive arms of c.eligible; the review acknowledgement follows the human review step and carries no route by design. The decision SLA runs from the request.
Keyed on the request. A rejected request is an invalid state, not a failure of validation.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the obligation. Pure router by design: resources exist or they do not.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the allocation. The wait is bound to the reservation's own expiry.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the obligation.
Keyed on the exception. Pure router by design: every resolution belongs to another journey.

The no-choice update and the offer are the exclusive arms of c.choice; the offer carries the choices. At most two touches. Pure router by design: every ending belongs to execution, exception, cancellation or ownership. Outcome: fulfilment resuming.
Keyed on the dispatch. Pure router by design: the executor's outcome decides the next journey.
Keyed on the delivery attempt. The correction request and the alternatives offer each carry their route. Both waits are response windows from the touch. Pure router by design.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the obligation and the delivery. Both waits are bound to the policy windows.
A completed reconciliation is the success of this journey.

The acceptance request follows the arrival confirmation directly, not through the delivery wait - the drafted gate was wrong. The arrival confirmation carries no route by design; the acceptance request carries the accept-or-raise route. The delivery wait is the executor's own window; the acceptance wait is bound to the acceptance window. The longest path sends three touches. Outcome: acceptance.

Keyed on the obligation and the offer. The offer and the reminder carry the accept-or-decline route; the two confirmations are the exclusive arms of c.answer and the lapse notice closes the offer - none of the three carries a route by design. Both waits are bound to the offer's closing date. A decline is a failure of the substitution, not a no-action. The longest path sends three touches.
Keyed on the issue. Attachment to an existing case is a suppression; no remedy owed is a no-action outcome.
Keyed on the return request. Rejection, authorisation and review are the exclusive arms of c.eligible; the authorisation carries the return instructions. At most two touches reach the requester.
Named the proxies. Keyed on the correction. The wait is bound to the correction's deadline. Pure router by design.
Keyed on the issue. The options message carries the options; the no-remedy statement carries the appeal route it names. The selection wait is a response window from the touch.
Keyed on the relationship record.
Named the proxies. The pre-start wait runs to the effective time. Not activating at the effective date is a failure.
The scheduled-change wait runs to the change's effective time. A rejected or not-applied change leaves the terms as they were: invalid-state outcomes.
Accepted as drafted.
Named the proxies.
The suspension wait is bound to the maximum duration policy defines.
Reaching the terminal state is the success of this journey; the wind-down wait is an observation window.

The confirmation carries no route by design. The window wait is bound to the effective end date. Ending cleanly is the success; a withdrawn cancellation is an invalid state for this journey, which never re-litigates. No business outcome: the journey exists to make the end date unsurprising, not to win anyone back.
Keyed on the hold. Consumption into a confirmed reservation is the hold's success.
Keyed on the reservation request.
Keyed on the booking and the reschedule request. No move taking place is a failure of the request, with the original preserved.
A clean cancellation is the success of this reconciliation.
Accepted as drafted.
Accepted as drafted.
Keyed on the booking and the provider failure. The reallocation notice is informational and carries no route by design. A provider-side cancellation is a failure of the commitment, recorded as ours.

Confirmation, re-offer and decline are the exclusive arms of c.outcome; the re-offer carries the slots and the choice wait is bound to the choosing deadline. The lapse notice follows the acknowledgement. At most two touches reach one requester.

Keyed on the person and the availability query. An unprompted offer after a search is commercial recovery: promotional pressure, in the commerce-recovery group. The offer and the waitlist are the exclusive arms of c.options and each carries its route. The settle wait is a recovery window from the query. Exit classes corrected. Outcome compared pre/post.

Keyed on the decision case and the requirement. The external and internal requests are the exclusive arms of c.source-type; the external request carries where to provide the item. Requests repeat only within the request budget policy allows, so the local cap is that budget - a required config. The wait is bound to the information deadline. A moot case is an invalid state; closure for want of information is a timeout.

Keyed on the decision. Correctable, reapplicable and final are the exclusive arms of c.path; the correctable and reapply statements carry their paths, the cleared confirmation and the expiry notice follow the correctable statement and carry none by design. The remediation wait is bound to the correction deadline. At most two touches. A decision that stands is a failure outcome for the subject, stated honestly. Outcome: correction, compared pre/post.

Keyed on the entity, the limit and the window. A usage limit is service communication, not security. Only the wall notice and the reset notice are mandatory; the offers are discretionary. Self-offer and holder-offer are the exclusive arms of c.decider, and the blocked-party notice follows the holder-offer; both offers carry the capacity route. The capacity wait is bound to the window's reset. Blocked with no route is a no-action state.
Keyed on the version and the recipient. The distribution wait is the delivery mechanism's own window.
Keyed on the lineage and the conflict.

The actionable and standing notices are the exclusive arms of c.usable; the actionable notice and the reminder carry the first action. The reminder is discretionary. The dormancy wait is bound to the effective period. Ended without use is an invalid state; dormant is a timeout. Outcome compared pre/post.

Keyed on the target and the change. The hold notice and the blocker prompt are the exclusive arms of c.resolvable; the blocker prompt and the last call carry the clearing route. Both waits are bound to the preparation window. Two prompts at most, per the corpus. Outcome: the prerequisite cleared, compared pre/post.
Keyed on the incident, the cohort and the state change. Nothing material to say is a no-action outcome.
